output.subject: We have received your message about your joint account
output.body:
Hello,

We were very sorry to read of your wife's passing, and we are sorry for the added stress you have described at such a difficult time. Thank you for writing to us.

We have received your complaint and want to confirm what you told us. You mentioned that you and your wife held a joint checking account with us for over thirty years. Since her death on July 27th, you have visited the Elm & 4th branch three times, and you told us that each visit you were asked for a different document: first the death certificate, then a letter from the funeral home, and then a small estate affidavit. You mentioned that the account is now restricted, that you cannot reach the $4,210.55 in it, and that you have the funeral bill and your own bills to pay. You also told us your wife always handled the banking.

You asked for one complete list of everything we need, and for access to the funds in the account.

A specialist team is reviewing your complaint and will respond within 10 business days.

With our sincere condolences,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: The ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧ token in this complaint refers to the deceased wife, not the writer. The greeting was left as 'Hello,' so the letter is not addressed to her. Insert the surviving husband's name before sending.
⟦NAME_1⟧ also appears to refer to the wife. Confirm the identities of both tokens before personalizing.
Confirm whether the account was held jointly with right of survivorship. This affects which documents are actually required.
The customer explicitly wants one complete document list. Decide whether the response can provide it.
Review why three branch visits produced different document requests.
The customer reports urgent financial need for funeral costs and bills. Consider whether hardship or bereavement support applies.
The customer is newly bereaved and says his wife handled all banking. Use plain, gentle language in follow-up and consider offering a single point of contact.
Check whether any deceased-customer correspondence suppression is needed so future mail is not addressed to the wife.
